Hi Sofia / Chris —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture the key points from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. High-level summary below — please reply with any corrections or additions.

Pain points / goals
- Primary concern: PII and sensitive fields showing up in model logs and audit traces — must limit exposure for regulated customers.
- Need configurable retention for request/response logs (different retention windows for PII vs. telemetry).
- Strong requirement for auditable deletion and retention policies (legal/regulatory review).
- Want the ability to redact or mask parts of requests before they hit any persistent logs; also need an audit trail of redaction actions.

Current stack (from today)
- Ingest pipeline: AWS Kinesis -> S3 -> Snowflake for analytics.
- Application: customer service chat + automated summarization (some PHI/PII in transcripts).
- Security: FinFlex manages its own KMS; SOC 2 Type II mandated.

Success criteria for proof-of-concept (PoC)
- Demonstrate configurable log retention (30/90/365 days) per data class (PII vs non-PII).
- Show redaction/masking capability for request prefixes and selective fields prior to persistence.
- Ability to integrate with FinFlex KMS and provide audit logs for accesses and deletions.
- Provide SOC2 evidence and dataflow diagrams for internal security review.

Agreed next steps
1) I will share a SOC2 summary and a high-level dataflow diagram (attached).
2) Schedule a technical/security deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer + FinFlex security team — proposed: Tue, Jun 30, 10:00 AM PT.
3) FinFlex to send any existing security questionnaire or specific retention/PII language to review.
4) If PoC looks good, we will outline MA redlines and a mutual action plan.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf, dataflow-diagram.png

Marissa

Sofia — great questions. Quick answers here and then we can dig into details on the deep-dive.

- Default logging behavior: Redwood can be configured. By default our hosted API retains request/response logs for 90 days for telemetry and troubleshooting (including metadata). For customers with stricter requirements we support configurable modes:
  * Full logs (default): request text + model output + metadata for 90 days
  * Metadata-only: persist only request/response hashes and operational metadata (no plaintext)
  * Redacted-mode: request text persists but PII fields are redacted/masked before storage.

- Retention windows: configurable per data class. We can set PII retention to 30 days for the PoC and non-PII to 90/365 as needed.

- Redaction/masking: We support SDK-side pre-processing hooks and server-side redaction. Options include prefix masking, regex-based field redaction, and deterministic hashing for identifiers. We can also provide a policy to automatically detect common PII types and redact by default.

- KMS & encryption: Customer-managed KMS integration is supported for dedicated/private deployments. Access to logs is logged and exported to audit streams; we can produce an access report as part of the PoC.

Attachments: data-retention-policy.docx (attached) — contains implementation options and examples of retention configurations. I’ve also uploaded our SOC2 summary and the dataflow diagram to the HubSpot deal for your team.

Proposed next steps (concrete)
- Security deep-dive: Tue, Jun 30, 10:00 AM PT — Solutions Engineer (Rishi) + Security SMEs from FinFlex. Can you confirm attendees?
- We’ll prepare short write-ups for: (a) retention options and cost impact, (b) redaction strategies and sample SDK snippets, (c) contract language examples for deletion/retention.
